import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import os
import hashlib
import lightgbm as lgb
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)
os.makedirs("submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
print("Loading data...")
train = pd.read_csv("input/train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("input/test.csv")
sample_submission = pd.read_csv("input/sample_submission.csv")

# Features
target_col = "target"
drop_cols = ["id", "target"]
feature_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c not in drop_cols]


# Preprocessing: Handle f_27 high cardinality
def hash_encode(x):
    s = str(x) if pd.notna(x) else ""
    return int(hashlib.md5(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(), 16) % 1000


train["f_27"] = train["f_27"].apply(hash_encode)
test["f_27"] = test["f_27"].apply(hash_encode)

# Define columns for squared features (excluding f_28 which has much larger range)
squared_cols = [
    c
    for c in feature_cols
    if c not in ["f_27", "f_28", "f_29", "f_30"]
    and train[c].dtype in ["float64"]
    and c
    not in [
        "f_07",
        "f_08",
        "f_09",
        "f_10",
        "f_11",
        "f_12",
        "f_13",
        "f_14",
        "f_15",
        "f_16",
        "f_17",
        "f_18",
    ]
]

for col in squared_cols:
    train[f"{col}_sq"] = train[col] ** 2
    test[f"{col}_sq"] = test[col] ** 2

# Prepare features
X_train = train[feature_cols + [f"{c}_sq" for c in squared_cols]]
X_val = train[feature_cols + [f"{c}_sq" for c in squared_cols]]
y_train = train[target_col]
y_val = train[target_col]

# Split train into train/val (80/20)
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train, y_train, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
)

# Define LightGBM parameters (same as baseline)
params = {
    "objective": "binary",
    "metric": "auc",
    "boosting_type": "gbdt",
    "num_leaves": 31,
    "learning_rate": 0.05,
    "feature_fraction": 0.9,
    "bagging_fraction": 0.8,
    "bagging_freq": 5,
    "verbose": -1,
    "n_jobs": -1,
    "random_state": 42,
}

# Create Dataset
train_data = lgb.Dataset(X_train, label=y_train)
val_data = lgb.Dataset(X_val, label=y_val, reference=train_data)

# Train model
print("Training model...")
model = lgb.train(
    params,
    train_data,
    num_boost_round=500,
    valid_sets=[val_data],
    callbacks=[lgb.early_stopping(stopping_rounds=50), lgb.log_evaluation(0)],
)

# Predict on validation set
val_pred = model.predict(X_val, num_iteration=model.best_iteration)
val_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, val_pred)

# Predict on test set
test_features = feature_cols + [f"{c}_sq" for c in squared_cols]
test_pred = model.predict(test[test_features], num_iteration=model.best_iteration)

# Create submission
submission = sample_submission.copy()
submission.loc[:, "target"] = test_pred

# Save submission
submission.to_csv("submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print(f"Validation AUC: {val_auc:.5f}")
plan: I will enhance the baseline model by creating squared features for the main continuous columns (f_00 through f_06 and f_19 through f_26), which directly captures curvature relationships rather than just magnitude. This is distinct from the absolute value features previously added, as squared terms allow tree models to learn parabolic relationships that may be important for manufacturing state prediction. Tree-based models can split on squared features to capture non-linear magnitude effects more effectively.
